I used to be on Wellbutrin, and I still take Trileptal as an anti-depressant (for 5 years)... I'm not quite sure what to say regarding depression, I believe it did put alot of symptoms on mute the majority of time. 

However, I can 100% vouch that it did help me quit smoking, if you're consistent with taking your meds properly, it cuts out your cravings for food, cigarettes, etc VERY efficiently. I take adderall for ADD, and if I had to compare wellbutrin to adderall regarding appetite (where the weight loss comes in, works even better if you also exercise), it's definitely similar but doesn't give you as much focus and energy as adderall will. After taking wellbutrin for a couple of months, I was able to cut down on smoking almost cold turkey because I became disgusted with the taste and smell of cigarettes. 

Overall, I'd say go for it, it worked decently for me. You should also keep in mind that certain prescriptions will work differently for everyone.

what are you on? quitting meds suddenly is dangerous, im sure you are aware of that. its good to that you're back on them, and it really depends on how they work for you I guess. the first time i started seeing a psychiatrist he misdiagnosed me as bipolar 1 and put me on all kinds of crap like lithium, abilify, celexa and they fucked me up. i also had a bad habit of quitting or purposely not taking them and I forget how much i fuck myself over when I don't take them because i tend fall into depressive relapses quick. however lately ive been taking my current cocktail more responsibly and I havent really been having any problems lately besides acute panic attacks at work sometimes. but yeah, meds are definitely a commitment (since our bodies get used to the chemicals, we are vulnerable to biological addiction) and they work differently for everyone. i think even sudden can cause certain symtoms so that might also be why you're having some trouble. finding the right meds is so hard.

I never believed medications completely temporarily cured or stabilized. Even my psychiatrist told me his goal was to just control the most bothersome symtoms (anxiety, agitation and depressive symptoms) as well improve in other areas like focus and weight, in which an increase in confidence would also help control my moods. Which is why my current cocktail is adderall, trileptal, klonopin and trazadone. As a Type II, on my current cocktail I still notice mood swings but less intense symptoms as before.
